questions.q: What is the author's main argument?
options: Politics and religion should never be discussed in any forum
Identity-driven topics ruin discussion, so keep your identity small
Only experts should be allowed to post opinions on online forums
Programming languages cannot be compared because all are equally good
questions.explain: Discussions fail when they engage identity, so one should let as few things as possible into one's identity.

questions.q: Why does the author say religion threads grow faster than Javascript threads?
options: Religion threads attract more experts who argue about doctrine
Forum moderators ban Javascript talk but allow religious topics
People feel no expertise is needed to have opinions on religion
Javascript is less interesting to most people who use forums
questions.explain: On religion, all you need is strongly held beliefs, so there is no expertise threshold.

questions.q: Which example does the author use to show identity depends on people, not topic?
options: A baking contest versus a Javascript tutorial
A Bronze Age battle versus a modern battle
A tax policy debate versus a cost estimate
A chess match between two famous grandmasters
questions.explain: A modern battle with citizens involved turns political, while a Bronze Age battle wouldn't.

questions.q: What harmless-seeming topic does he say can't safely be discussed with some people?
options: Apple versus Android phones
Coke versus Pepsi soft drinks
Ford versus Chevy pickup trucks
Yankees versus Red Sox baseball
questions.explain: He notes the relative merits of Ford and Chevy pickups can't be safely discussed with others.

questions.q: What would the author likely say about the debate over programming languages?
options: It is unanswerable because all languages are equally good
It can be fruitful if identity-driven responders are excluded
It should be avoided entirely, as it always becomes a war
Only expert programmers should join in any such discussion
questions.explain: He says you can have a fruitful discussion about languages if you exclude people who respond from identity.
